A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same CGNN research. All pages, tables, figures, equations and appendices are available and readable; v2's Section 8 corresponds to v4's Appendix A.

before.justification: v2 reports original node-classification experiments on eight datasets, accuracy and runtime comparisons, and component analyses in Section 6.

after.justification: v4 retains these original experimental results, including Table 2's classification results and the analyses in Tables 3–6 and Figure 3.

M1.justification: Sections 5.1–5.4 and Algorithm 1 retain the same DiLap formulation, similarity-based rewiring, randomized SVD computation, commute-time weighting and directional aggregation procedure.

E1.justification: Both evaluate node classification on the same eight datasets with identical dataset statistics. v4's 'citepseer' is a typo for Citeseer, not different coverage. Fraud detection is added only as an introductory application example.

E2.justification: Table 2 retains the same 13 baseline rows, including DUPLEX, DiGCL and DirGNN. Figure 3's comparator set and the CGNNppr and CGNNsym comparisons also remain unchanged.

E3.justification: Both specify the same accuracy metric, 48%/32%/20% public splits for Squirrel and Chameleon, and 20 training nodes per class plus 500 validation nodes for other datasets. Symmetrization controls and component-analysis procedures are unchanged.

E4.justification: Both contain the same heterophily-distance analysis, rewiring-versus-PPR comparison, commute-time preservation analysis and directed-versus-undirected ablation in Tables 3–6. No analysis is added or removed.

E5.justification: Both report classification accuracy with standard deviation over 10 runs in Table 2 and identify the same 10 public splits. No seed, repeated-run or uncertainty-reporting practice changes.

E6.justification: All numerical entries in Tables 1, 2 and 4–6 match, and Table 3's bars and Figure 3's plotted results are unchanged. For example, CGNN retains 77.61 ± 1.87 on Squirrel and 92.89 ± 0.51 on Roman-Empire.

T1.justification: The assumptions, propositions, theorems and mathematical definitions are unchanged. v2 Sections 8.1–8.3 match v4 Appendices A.1–A.3, including the DiLap derivation, Lemma 5.1 proof and SVD equations; only formatting and references change.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction and conclusion retain the same contributions: efficient DiLap-based commute-time computation and its integration into directional message passing. The stated experimental superiority and six-of-eight-datasets finding remain unchanged.

C2.justification: Section 6 retains the same explanations concerning heterophily filtering, rewiring and directed structure. The application-scope discussion still qualifies usefulness on citation networks lacking reciprocal paths and favors networks with mutual relationships.

D1.justification: The disclosed hardware, typical SVD rank q = 5, normalization, pseudocode and implementation-related procedures are unchanged. No implementation resource or code/data access information is added or removed.

R1.justification: v4 adds four introductory citations: Zhuo and Tan (2022a, 2022b, 2023) and Zhuo et al. (2024), covering graph similarity, proximity-based learning and fraud detection. Existing related-work discussions and novelty positioning otherwise remain unchanged.

P1.justification: The narrative and section order are largely identical. v4 changes author/affiliation information, switches to author–year citations and an alphabetical bibliography, relabels Section 8 as Appendix A, and introduces the repeated 'citepseer' typo.

P2.justification: v4 applies a document-wide layout change: a narrower text block, revised title/author arrangement, removed dated running headers, and resized and reflowed figures, tables and algorithm. Tables 1 and 2 are grouped together, while the plots move to the following page. Graphical content itself is retained.

improvement.justification: v4 preserves the same scientific contribution, experimental evidence, interpretations and appendix proofs. Added introductory citations and extensive reformatting do not materially change the paper's overall quality. The new 'citepseer' typo is a small editorial flaw, but the dataset remains identifiable and the results are unaffected.
